title: Rome Odunze, Tyrique Stevenson, Jonah Jackson discuss approach during OTAs | Press Conference
text: Hey, birthday bro. >> Thank you. Appreciate that. Yeah, man. Kobe here. >> Nothing much. I mean, obviously we cooking during the week, but probably go down to city, get myself a nice dinner um over the weekend. So, that's about it. >> Last season, you had expressed some disappointment in the way your year went. What was your process of resetting and getting yourself back up to speed? >> Yeah, just going back to work really. Uh obviously you got to take a break away from the game a little bit, you know, especially with uh kind of the injuries and stuff I had last year. Had to take my time and um you know, talk to the training staff, talk to my own team as well. Just getting on the same page and getting as healthy as possible um in that window and also trying to gear back up to get ready for for this period of training and and the next season of course. So um it it was really just back to work. Um and to start off that was more just rehab and um getting the foot right, getting the body right. How frustrating was it after you had such a fast start to the season to then have an injury and kind of take a hit in your progression after that? >> It was tough. It was tough. Obviously, you know, I was gearing up for for a great season. I felt like, you know, it was on track to to to have that. Um and you know, injuries are part of the game and unfortunately I feel like it affected me um you know, more than injuries have in the in the past. Uh and and that wasn't um you know obviously the goal you know I have my goals before the season and that injury kind of prohibited some of those things but it's part of the game and it's things that you know you work through and you go through that adversity and you're better for it. >> You go through some of the frustration that you've had over your first two seasons not being where you've wanted to be production wise. What specific elements of your game do you identify and say these are things that have to get better for me in year three? Um, I mean, I feel like for me, I'm trying to be excellent in every single category of wide receiver, you know, um, route running, releases, catching the football. Um, there there's areas of improvement in every single rep, you know, out there that like it's hard to pinpoint one thing. I want to do everything excellent. So, I'm trying to improve on all those different factors all at once. Um, because I feel like I'm capable of doing that. Is there any any of those that you feel like you have been consistently good at and any that have been consistently kind of problematic for you? >> Um, honestly, no. Honestly, no. I feel like, you know, I've kind of been um obviously there's certain things that I feel like I do well, but um to me, the art of wide receiver is the whole thing. You know what I mean? You can't have you can't be a good wide receiver that only runs good routes but doesn't catch the ball. You can't you can't be a good wide receiver that doesn't run any good routes but also only catches the ball. You know what I'm saying? you kind of have to have a plethora of all those different aspects to to um play football, you know, play the wide receiver position and and it encompasses it all as a whole. So, no, >> when we talked to Antoine Randall a couple weeks ago, I said you guys watched tape of some of those catches that you didn't make last year. Um maybe saw some things in that. What do you think you learned from from looking back at that? >> Um honestly, just making the play in the moment. Um I feel like I put in the work to to make those things happen. um you know I practice you know heavily on all those different aspects of catching the football catch point um contested catches all those different things. So um the work is there I think you know when the obviously you got to double down on those things and when the results don't kind of show the the what what the work uh that was put in um the work that was put in doesn't show the results that kind of um um should should be there you just double down on that's kind of what I'm doing >> did you sense that any of that was concentration in the moment with with some of those missed opportunities? Um, you could say concentration. Um, it's hard to pinpoint exactly, you know, um, what it is. I feel like I'm pretty concentrated in those moments, but um, you know, there there's a level of concentration and laps in those things. I feel like in any aspect of it that you can kind of consider, but um, for me, I don't think it was a concentration aspect. Now, >> what do you what do you see as now an opportunity with DJ no longer in the room and kind of being that number one target? >> Yeah, I mean, for me, I think it's the room as a collective. You know, when I came in and it was Keenan and DJ, it was the collective. When I when I came in and Keenan left and Luther came in, it was DJ. Three of us, it was the collective. Now that DJ's gone, it's the collective group. So, for me, you know, I just want to be the best receiver possible for this team. I feel like I provide many assets to do that. Um, and I'm comfortable with a lot of the target share as well as the other guys getting involved so we can be the best offense possible. >> You get Leaf and Scotty a little bit better this spring. What do you hope to pick from their brains just knowing they've played a lot of football? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, anything, anything really. Um, you know, their longevity in the league, you know, how they take care of their bodies, all those things. Obviously, um, you know, I'm an older receiver in the room, but I'm still feel like younger in my receiver years. So, um, just trying to take anything I can from those guys. Um, um, when it comes to routes and and shifting this, they're they're a little bit smaller than me. So, um, you know, we have a kind of different, but Leaf got a crazy stride. So, you know, there's things I can I can take from them, but uh um but yeah, no, I mean, they're vets in the room, so those are my guys. I'm definitely looking to learn a few things. >> What does that what does that breakout look like for you in terms of whether it's numbers or production in your mind? What does that look like to you? >> I think it's everything. It's everything. It's it's wins. It's it's numbers. It's when I go when we watch film in the meeting rooms, it's the the pluses, you know, it it's all those different things. I don't want, you know, just to have a great a great individual season. Um, you know, I I want to collectively be a tremendous wide receiver that has a tremendous impact on with his team that get gets wins week in and week out. >> Perspective on the opportunity for this offense where you've got a young ascending quarterback, you've got yourself, Luther, Coloulston all on the rise. How do you view it when you're out here working on where you guys want to go? >> Man, I view it as like we like a young core, you know? We like some just some hungry dogs in this league, you know, ready to get after it really. Um, you know, we got a lot of young players that um have a lot on our on our plates and, you know, I feel like that's good for us, you know, um and and maybe expectation of young players in this leagues is like mental and and different mistakes like that. I think we're we're excited for the opportunity and trying to exceed expectations for for younger players in this league in this younger core. So, um you know, the goal is the Lombardi Trophy regardless of where they're at and and and that's every single year. Going back to Dan's question about focus on the drop. Do you think that that was component with the injury while you kind of nursing as you run through your route trying to figure out how to plan how to do this that's on your mind? You think that takes your focus away for just a second and maybe cause some of that? >> You know, I think I think there was definitely a little bit of that. Um, you know, I I was rehabbing the foot. I've never had really, you know, injury like that before that was kind of um prohibiting me in that way. But, you know, I'm the I'm the type of person at the same time that don't want to provide those excuses for myself at the end of the day. So, it's like, you know, if the ball's not caught, the ball's not caught regardless if I'm running on one foot or whatever it is. So, that's my standard and that's my expectation and I didn't do it well enough. >> Is that is that fully >> 100% and and is it something that's will continually have to be monitored and stuff? >> I mean, I feel like if you break a bone, you always got to, you know, make sure you on top of it. You know, I continue to do rehab on it, make sure I'm keeping it strong, and that's both feet. um whether it comes to, you know, the um different exercises that they they give me and the rehab as well that I do um off the field. But um I feel like yeah, you you got to stay on top of it. Um regardless of if it's a 100 or not, I feel like I'm it's hard to say it's like a 100. I feel like when it's when we're win the Super Bowl and we win that and and we raise that trophy, it'll be 100. >> What was your reaction to? >> Yeah. >> What was the point where it felt normal to you to run on it? felt normal. Felt usual. Um, this is my new normal. This is my new normal. Um, and and it's not from a standpoint that I'm like always in pain, but the way my foot broke, there's a callus in there that like creates, you know, a different type of foot structure with those bones, different things. It kind of um um, you know, shifts things around. So, I my new normal was kind of what I, you know, am growing into. Um, and I don't think that's anything that's gonna prohibit me or or keep me from from making plays, but I feel like with with the break, it's just like, you know, when you tear your AC, it's never really back to normal. You're Shout out to Keenan with his, you know, his little, you know what I'm saying? It's a little different, but we we go on. >> Did you ever need surgery? >> I ever need surgery? Um, it's it's it was a it was a question. It was a question. I feel like the the doctors advised that it was um uh something that that we can monitor, but they definitely felt like it was able to heal without surgery. So, um, you know, that's kind of the process I went towards just because, you know, I don't like putting any metal or rods into my foot. So, um, yeah, it was, uh, it was a question, but I feel like the process we went was adequate. >> What was your reaction to Caleb on the cover, man? And what do you think about >> Oh, I loved it. I loved it. Yeah. No, I mean, he had a spectacular season, and, you know, the the the cover was dope. His little uh MJ kind of tribute. Um, I know the Chicagoans are are happy to see that one. Kind of a throwback. It was pretty cool. So, um, you know, I don't really play Madden that much, but I got to play this year to see what animations they put in for his throws. And I know it's like, you know, that little under toss throw that that Patrick Mahomes had a few years ago. So, yeah, that was dope. Do >> you consider yourself kind of on the cover since that throw was to you? >> Say that again. >> Do you consider you like you were kind of on the cover since that throw was to you? >> Yeah. Yeah. Uh, basically I'm like, yeah, I'm going to tell my kids like, "Yeah, he's on the cover, but he's throwing the ball." >> Oh, no, no, no. I don't count that, man. I want to get on the cover of my damn self. So, Harris said a couple weeks ago that you felt like your your focus was at a all new level this year. Can you kind of describe where you're at with with your mindset? >> Uh I would say it's just more of a uh just honing in on the small details of my game. You know, uh playing corner, you give up certain things. You you're not good at certain things. So, I'm just trying to come in after every practice and hone in on the small details. Uh I ask most of the offensive coaches like, "If you had to go at me, what what' you see?" And so I I just think like my attentions to detail is is just being a little bit more um paid attention to and and it's making the coaches happy. >> Have you done that before? Have you done that before? Talk to offensive coaches like that or is this the first time you've done that? >> Uh it's kind of like the first time I did it. Um I just want to know where I can get better to help this team and go out there and perform at a high level. >> The way last year ended with uh you maybe not getting as many reps as you you wanted. Did that motivate you into your offseason? >> Uh I'm always motivated going into my offseason. Uh I will be real that that the Hail Mary was the top of the top. So I'm always motivated now. But um no, I just uh understand the coach's decision. Everything uh happens for a reason. I trust these co I trust the guys on this team and I trust the staff. So just wanted to uh come and just prove prove myself to myself this year. So >> anything you could share with us specifically that they told you that they see more of for you to play more because >> it it was it was nothing specific. I would say uh probably a big thing just staying focused. uh staying locked in on the small details and making sure that you know every time I step on the field it's with a it's with a purpose. >> How different does it feel as much turnover as there's been in the secondary and some faces that aren't here anymore? >> H it's weird but it's it's good though. Uh I would say you know um just from when I got here Eddie leaving and everything like that. So it's kind of I'm I'm kind of used to it now but it's just uh it's definitely weird but I'm definitely happy with the guys they brought in. U I feel like we clicking as a group and we looking forward to going be the best secondary in the league again. KB was such a big leader back there. Where do you think that leadership who takes on that? I guess is it a collective thing? Is there somebody you think that's going to stand out and take on that role? >> Uh that's that's really for training camp to see right now is OTAAS. We got new guys so everybody's filling everybody out and um uh I think you know just the guy who needs to be that is going to rise to the top. >> Early impressions of both Kobe and and the man behind you >> fast. Fast. Uh Kobe knows ball pretty much you know. Um, we be just talking my locker right next to his. We just be talking and just to hear him talk nothing but ball and we can articulate it the same is just giving me confidence in knowing that I got him behind me. >> Last couple weeks ago we had a chance to talk to Al Harris and he he really took accountability for um last year specifically when it came to you. Have you noticed any type of like uptick with him and attention coaching your relationship with him? Anything different so far this year? Uh, not really. It was the same. It was kind of the same last year, but I would say, uh, going into this year, uh, you know, they looking for me to be a bigger role. So, I say it's just a lot more conversations about what I'm not doing to, uh, what I'm not doing and how I'm performing. So, I say just a lot more conversations in that area. But, it's been pretty much the same. Relationship was always good. Conversations about what I need to do for this team has always been there. So, I just think like I was saying earlier, just the we we talk more about the small details instead of the bigger picture. >> So, it's really just like the communication. >> Yes. Yes. >> Gotcha. you set intentions for yourself like for this season, just knowing you're going into a contract year. How do you approach that? >> Uh just approach it one step every day. You know, um the best thing I could do is come out here, be available, and and be a good teammate, and also go out there and do my job. And honestly, that's how I'm looking at it. >> Can you give us an example of a small detail you've been working on? >> I would say uh just something like coming out my breaks, like not doing too many steps. Receiver talked out out of the third step, he should be coming out of break. I have to be a better athlete, so it should be like two and a half or I should be able to match his step. So, something like small like that to where it can give me uh a good chance to go pick the ball. >> T El has a track record of of getting ball production out of a lot of different guys no matter where he's been. What is it about him that that gets guys to reach new levels? >> I'll say he he builds confidence in attacking the ball. Like, um you know, as a DB sometimes you don't turn your head around, you just play through the hands. The PBU is good, but without the PBU ain't nothing. Uh he wants the ball. So, I think him speaking it every day, him giving us goals, we need three every practice, we need three every practice. I think it just builds the confidence to once we know what the route is, go play the route and and make sure you come down with the ball. >> How much credibility does he have given given all the guys that he's taken to to new heights? He has a lot. Um, you know, like you said, with the guys he's had, his his his uh his record shows that if you trust him and you believe him, you play the game the the right way he's teaching it, you u you'll either like Shnie did last year, you'll be your lead or you'll be at the top when it comes down to interceptions. >> We headed into the offseason thinking he would have a lot of interest to maybe be a defensive coordinator somewhere and he said, "No, I want to stay here." What does that mean just kind of to your group that >> uh definitely cherish it? Um because that mean you know he came back for a reason. He came back because he believed in these coaching staff. He believed in the guys in the building. And you know, just for him to be able to depart and not leave, I just cherish it, you know, to come back and get coached up by him and, you know, take some more details so I can take my game to the next level. >> What makes this receiver group maybe I don't perhaps the most challenging you had to go against, you know, in practice? >> They all rolling. They all rolling. They all are fast and they all are uh coming down with, you know, with some of the catches Caleb throwing. You know, even if that's across the middle, they have they have strong hands. is they they can run any route on the route tree pretty much and I think that's just getting us better as a secondary. >> Is that fair to say this is the toughest group that you've had to go against in in house? >> I I would say but uh my rookie DJ gave me a run for my money every practice. So I would say just in total the group. Yes. Yes. >> From a defensive perspective, how would you describe Caleb and Rome's uh connection? >> It's great. It's all I feel like since they got here has always been that. Um, but I would just say like uh Rome stepping into that uh into that role, you know, Rome down there somewhere guy. So, uh, it's definitely going good. Caleb giving Rome the opportunity to make plays and, uh, definitely like their relationship is doing great. >> Tyreek, do do you feel some, uh, do you feel a responsibility to be vocal because half your starting defense wasn't here last year and doesn't know a DA system? Uh, do you try to act like a veteran a little bit to help them uh, pick stuff up? Uh, I would say somewhat. Yeah. Um, I feel like for me to to to to be able to help this defense, I should be able to be vocal. Uh, without even the vet part being added to it, I think I should be vocal, you know, with our calls, with our communications. That way, it give guys, like you said, who haven't been here, give them the confidence to play fast. So, we all moving fast. But, uh, I definitely try to do my part in my in the DB room of relaying information and receiving it and try to distribute it amongst the guys. >> If you got a peak in the Madden cover today. Yeah, >> it's tough. It's tough. I told him he got signs. I I don't want He got signs. Uh definitely proud of him for that though. That that's that's I'm I'm actually honored to be on the team with somebody on the mat and cover. So, >> what did he do last year to give you guys the the feeling that you're in good hands? We just knew. We just knew honestly um towards the end of the season coming out to the third quarter, we just it was like knowing that he's going to turn it on and just knowing that as long as we we stay to our rules, we play our game, we have a chance at every game. >> What you going to do with DJ when you all go to Buffalo? That's all that matters. >> What's the process like getting to getting to work in the new center? I know you guys can't ps or anything like that, but it's like creating cohesive. >> Um yeah, I mean like I feel like um having Garrett in there um he's been in the league now for eight years. A lot of schemes and things he's been around is very similar to what we do and he's a smart guy and um Joe had a lot of familiar familiarity with him. So knowing that and getting to know him a little more I feel like it's been pretty easy jelling together. In what ways do you notice the offense being further ahead this spring than where you were a year ago? >> Um, I said this the other day, like the first week out, just breaking the huddle. You know, it was clean, crisp, cadence, everything. Um, guys are comfortable with what we're doing and, you know, the the scheme and understanding of things is the flow of practice has been much easier. A lot a lot of the conversation was around u not as focusing on as much scheme but focusing more on the technique. How have you noticed that and you guys preparation too? >> Yeah, I mean our our day-to-day indie doesn't change with coach Roshar and Kyle Dean. You know they're going to hammer the same thing day in and day out whether it's a deuce footwork everything. So you know technique's never been like uh somewhere we need to really focus on because we do it every day. Rashard gave you credit for being kind of the the voice in the O line room last year. What do you hope that you were able to bring and and show with a presence last year? >> Um, just some, you know, some energy, some juice, some confidence. You know, all O line rooms need that, especially with the job we have. Um, yeah, I feel like I feel like, you know, everybody plays their part and and that was mine. >> How much pride you guys take in Tuni winning the first ever Protector of the Year award? >> Nothing like it. It's awesome. Especially a guy like that, a decorated veteran. um a great guy on and off the field. Uh the the blueprint to what you want as not just an interior lineman, but an offensive lineman in general. And um yeah, him getting it was great. >> What's he do, Jonah? That that's most impressive to you. >> He's the same guy every single day. Probably the most consistent person outside of Ben that I've seen in in the league. Um yeah, he handles his busy. He's a grown-up. He's a he's a he's a pros pro. >> What have you seen from Braxton? You know, Ben said it feels like he's kind of the best shape he's been in. What's it like from Freepin for you to watch him work? >> Uh, yeah, when I got here last year, I think he was coming off some stuff. Um, but this year, I mean, he looks like a house he's moving well. Um, you know, just an indie, you know, we haven't really been able to go mono emano yet, but just his his movement and confidence in what he's doing has been exponentially different from last year. Logan comes from a place where that produces a lot of offensive linemen and like I know that kind of the pedigree of those Iowa guys are that they come in maybe more experienced than others. Like does that seem like that to you just from I mean I know he's a rookie but does he seem a little bit further along maybe? >> Yeah, definitely. He's a he's a mature guy. I think he's married so you know he's he's and he's he's been around for a while. Um yeah, he seems like a sharp tool and you know he'll be good for years to come. >> Being married doesn't mean you're mature. Maybe a little bit, you know. >> Did you grow up playing Did you grow up playing Madden? And did you see the You see the Caleb thing, too? >> I did. That's that's it's awesome, you know, especially having somebody. Is he the first bear I seen? Yeah. And the first bear and he's the first teammate I had ever on it. So, it's pretty cool. >> Anybody give him anybody bring it up to him today around you? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, everybody was congratulating him and stuff. You know, it's who doesn't want to be the cover of MA? You know, hopefully next year maybe they'll line get some love or something. appreciate what that says though just about his popularity and and his talent and what he's kind of brought to the league already. >> Um yeah, I mean especially being a city like Chicago, I feel like that that helps for sure. But him his caliber of player, the plays he made last year, the games he was able to help us win, it was a no-brainer who should have been on it. >> From your perspective, you understand the importance of year three for any player, but especially a quarterback in this league. Are are you curious to see kind of what Caleb's able to show off this year and build on from last year? Yeah, I mean he's still he's still developed and it's only year three. How old is he? 23 24, >> you know, most of these guys I've been around, they're they're 30 37. You know, I've been around some old guys. And to see his his growth from year one, year two, and then hopefully year two to year three is is is going to be special. >> Have you experienced him as a more vocal leader now compared to last year? >> I'd say he was pretty vocal last year. you know, um he was elected our our captain, not just cuz he's a quarterback, but the kind of guy he is and um how he goes about his business, but yeah, definitely hear more. >> What it mean to you to have a year that you had last year coming off what happened out in LA and there was some doubt about whether or not you could return to your previous season that you had. What that mean to you and what's the mentality that you come into this season? >> Um you know, it was it was big, you know, um just getting confidence back and and knowing what I'm able to do and and how I can contribute to the team and then, you know, I just want to build off it again. I'm in a still in my prime years. You know, I got some juice left in the tank, so I just want to build off >> Couple more. He had a a front row seat to watch Darnell kind of come into his own last year. What what struck you about the growth he made last year? >> I mean, he he he popped out on the tape when I was in uh Detroit and um seeing seeing working next to him, seeing how he works and his ability, you know, they call him the unicorn. He can he can do anything. And um I think this year ahead will be will be even better. Thank you.

title: OTA Interviews: Quinnen Williams, Tyler Booker, Rashan Gary & Donovan Ezeiruaku | Dallas Cowboys
text: the first full off season, first really workouts with the team. Just what have you kind of been focusing on and trying to just kind of get used to here? >> Uh really just personally getting better. Um personally just learning my craft. Um we got new new defensive staff, new defensive line coach, uh new pass, especially BT Jordan. um and just um feeding off them, learning and just crafting my craft right now and just trying to get as better I can so I can be um better than the years before and continue to grow, continue to um play well. Um, I just think it's uh beneficial when it come down to especially the defensive line dominancy when you kind of think about the 34 and the 4-3. You got more defensive linement on the field, which means more responsibility in that defensive line room. So, I I definitely enjoy that. I definitely enjoy CP and his mindset, the way he he do things, and also the defensive line coach and the way he do things. And I'm just super excited to continue to grow, continue to learn more, and continue to um perfect this scheme. So, Marcus Dixon had a short stint here as a as a player, but Cowboy fans really don't know anything about him as a position coach. What do they need to know about your new position? >> Oh, he's great. The last two weeks I've been with him, I've learned so much, especially getting back to this 34 scheme. Also, it's it's a great staff, a great room, and I'm super excited to to be a part of this new journey as u as a cowboy and his new defensive scheme, this defensive team. So, >> I'm sorry you weren't there, but can you tell us what you like about and and obviously the scheme about three, but what is where was they made in the offseason? What excites you about this team being better on defense? >> Uh, all the way around, man. Like you said, like 90% of this whole entire defensive defense, defensive staff is turned over and the guys we brought in from coaches all the way down as the player is unbelievable, man. And um the scheme itself, man, you got to see around the league, man. A lot of people running the same ski has unbelievable success. You got the Rams, you got Denver, you got the Philadelphia Eagles, and Seattle Seahawks kind of run the same similar scheme. So, um, New England Patriots kind of run the similar scheme. So, all the all the top defense in the league kind of running this scheme and uh super excited um the way that CP runs it, the the meticulous he is, man. The the detail he home in and uh to be around a great group of guys. So, >> I know it's a different I know it's a different position on defense, but with Caleb coming in, you're a former high draft pick, right? You know, the pressure. What can you share with a guy like that so that he's ready to go to start his NFL career off really well like you did? >> Yeah. >> Uh he has he has all the all the tools, man. um all the things that that you want in a guy to come in and make immediate impact on. He's humble, man. He's ready to learn. All the things you you see all the guys around the whole entire locker room. The guys they brought in from Casey to me to um Tito and all the other guys, man. So, um this a defense that we know we was bad last year and we know we need to get better this year cuz we we have a great offenses, man. And I've been a part of teams that that wasn't like that. And um it it's it's a blessing to have a great offense when you're on defense. And um so everybody on defense know how urgent it is is to get better. And having a guy like Caleb who's coming in with the same intensity and urgency for him to be an impact is unbelievable. So and he played among some great coaches in college and some great guys in college. So he knows how is to be to be a champion. So um having guys like that in the locker room who knows how to be a champion, knows how it's supposed to look and uh the right way is unbelievable to him. out here at the start of last year. How much do the two of you benefit from the snaps you get alongside one another? >> Oh, just having him in the room, I benefit tremendously from it, man. Just having a leader like he is, a player that he is, a guy who holds everybody accountable, and a guy who does everything right on the field and off the field. So, u that's first and foremost. But he's a dominant player, man. He's been a dominant player for years. I've been studying him for years and um just holding each other accountable to be the best we can be. We both still learning, both still growing and both want to be all pros and defensive player of the year candidates. Uh so keep pushing each other, keep holding each other accountable and um just keep trusting our coaches and the coaching staff to to to uh turn this thing around, especially on defense. How different is that? >> Uh, right now I'm just focused on the scheme itself. Not really my role in the scheme, just focusing on the scheme itself and doing the job best my ability and just homing in my craft or the things I did wrong last year and the things I want to get correct and u be better at. Um, so not really focus on my role in the scheme just yet, but just the scheme itself. >> What are the things? >> I think I can be better at pass rushing. I think I can um change up some of my game, change up some of my footwork. So >> does being settled help you individually too like you're not worrying about, hey, how do I get to this place or that place? You know, it all. >> Yeah. Yeah, it helps a lot. It helps a lot. Um they have a amazing staff here at this organization, man. They kind of take that load off, especially when I got traded last year. So that really wasn't a problem uh just because the staff that they have here that help me out every single day. But definitely ready to just get this thing going the right direction in a positive way. So >> how much improvement is it realistic to think you can make from one year to the next as a unit? >> As a unit tremendously. We was the bottom of the bottom. So it's like being the last of the last the bottom of the bottom. Um it's it's it's a lot of improvement that we can make and uh we got the right defensive staff um to make those improvement. we got the right guys in the locker room, drafted the right guys in the locker room um to get to get those improvement and um everybody taking full accountability to get that improved. What how much Can this team unit on the offensive line, I mean, how much better can it be this year compared to a year ago? >> I feel like we can be a lot better. So, very excited to go go to work with those guys this coming September. >> How does your bond with them growing off the field? What was it like there with that group? The photo went viral all >> Oh yeah. It was a lot of fun. Um so obviously we don't want him to peak right now and and we're not in that that mode but I like where how he's striking the football and he's he's going to be a big part of this deal. No, I like to I thought you were going to make fun of my arm and say you maybe you've seen better arms on a beanbag chair or something, you know. >> [laughter] >> No, you didn't like yeah and my hey, you can use that in your article. Um no, I I want to be around. The other part is is I get to be around the guys in a in their environment of offense and defense plus I mean football is football. I might I might see a skill the other day one of our corners crack replaced on an inside run which is the same technique he'd be using on kickoff and sometimes you might be able to say hey, what you just did right there that's a kickoff play and it kind of triggers for him and kind of gives him a little muscle memory so I I just I want to be around him as much as I can.

title: OC Bobby Slowik meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Well, obviously, it's a red zone day, so there should be a lot of touchdowns, but I'm glad to see that the offense is having some success. Do you contribute the mini camp successes you guys are having to no new installs and just repetitive things that coach is doing? >> Uh I think I think there's always multiple things at play, right? Like we've This will be the third time we had gone through the install at this point. Um you know, with very very little new wrinkles, but we got a lot of new faces out there, especially when it's a lot of seven-on-seven. There's a lot of new faces. So, you know, everybody kind of getting on the same page, knowing what they're doing. Uh you just can see the the confidence grow. And the big thing for us, I know I've said this before and I'll probably say it again through the course of of this is like this time of year is all about the individual, you know, like the fundamentals, the technique of what we're doing and trying to see that when you put a defense across from you. And you can't even get there if you don't really know what you're doing yet, you know? So, I think that definitely has helped um that we've chilled out once we got the base stuff in, we've chilled out and just let them go work. And then really just a lot of improvement across the board, you know, we still got a long way to go at every spot, but it it everybody's getting better, which has been fun to watch. >> What's the impression you get of the chemistry with this point with the offense and the receivers? A lot of these guys haven't worked together and they all play for the first time now. >> Yeah, it's an ongoing process, you know what I mean? And it's probably going to be an ongoing process all the way up to the regular season starts. That's how it always is. Uh there's a lot of people in and out right now, you know, there's a few guys Malik works with pretty consistently. Uh like Malik Washington, Tolbert's in there an awful lot, and then uh we try to mix it up here and there and get some fresh faces, so that's going to throw chemistry off. It's nice to see as we've kept banking reps through the off season, I feel like both the receivers and Malik have gotten more confident in what they're doing, where they're going to be, how different guys come out of breaks, you know, we throw routes on air and it's not going to be 100% completion yet in routes on air. Everybody comes out of different routes different. So, just getting the feel for that takes time. And they're doing the best they can. They're putting in work even even outside of what we ask them to do. So, it's it's just been a fun group to be a part of. >> I know it's early, but do you already see the benefit of doing the right side versus >> Uh I think you can see, you know, he's just confident. You know, I think he right now he's just confident what he's been doing. I do think there's a little bit of riding a bike. You know, he did the right side for so long, got used to the left, now going back to the right. He was excited about it, but there was a little bit of okay, is this going to be right away? How long is this going to take? And and I think he picked up the feel for really quickly, which has been fun to see. And he's dedicated a lot of time. You know, I think right or left, regardless of that right now for him, he's put in so much time to what he needs to improve upon. I would like to think it would have it would have gotten better anyway. So, I really like where he's at right now. >> With Quinn with Quinn yours, obviously you have experience from him from last year. He got those starts and those opportunities. The offense had a little bit of carryover for him. Um what steps do you hope that he takes in year two? >> Yeah, I've really liked, you know, what Quinn's done. And and the whole room, I think in the quarterback room in particular has really grown. Even for Quinn, you know, like you reference, there's some things we do that's the same, right? Uh and there's some things that we're going to do that are different. And then there's some things that we did last year that we'll just like talk about and coach differently. And I think that's harder than people realize, you know, when you have all these ingrained reps at this one thing, and then we're going to do the same thing but a little different. That takes longer than you would expect it to. And in particular the last 3 days, I really think you've seen Quinn take the next step of all right, I'm owning what this is right now. Let me take advantage of of kind of the little bit I already know and let me go out and just just play what I see and play convicted and let it rip. And I I would ask he does the same thing as we keep going through camp. You know, play disciplined, uh stick to the fundamentals as often as we can and then react to what you see and and a lot of times when he just goes and he plays and he reacts, he does some really cool stuff. Absolutely. You know, rarely do I coach to throw a blanketed check down. You know, that's that's usually not great ball. I'd probably with our group right now would if our check down's blanket, I'd say we got to go off schedule. You know, um I think it's a little bit it's it's interesting right now with our install. Like we actually have a pretty good balance of deep shots and some short throws and the intermediates. We're getting a lot of short throws and the intermediates right now. Uh and just the way our defense is kind of built, like the deep shots are hard to come by. That's kind of what they hang their hat on. Um so every now and then we try to get some going where, you know, we're going to push it and maybe we shouldn't push it, but we just need the reps at it. Uh but it the flip side it's flip side is it's like a great exercise for our quarterbacks. Like staying disciplined is one of the hardest things to do at that position, period, through the course of the season. It's hard to get over 70% completion. Like you have to be an extremely disciplined player. And them being able to get a whole lot of reps at that, I think we'll wind up benefiting us. >> Yeah, I you feel the size. Right? Like I think that's the biggest thing with Ali is not only is he big, he runs big. You know, when he's in the game and right now we don't have pads on, but when we have pads on like you're going to hear him run. It's not one where he's just going to silently kind of sneak through the line of scrimmage. You're everybody's going to feel uh it's going to sound like trash cans are banging back there. You know what I mean? And there there's something to that. Like the the old line gets energy from that when they feel the physicality from a runner. So, I think that's that's one thing he's always had, which we're always going to embrace. I really like with Ali like he's trying hard to take steps in the pass game and in pass pro. Like he's trying not to be just a uh uh run only back. And then really that's what he's working on right now and and he's been getting better at that every day, especially the protection aspect of it. You know, like that's a physical part of the game and it's a really important part of the game. And it's a mental challenge. And he's owning that part where now we can use him in a lot of different ways where every time he's on the field, we're not just running downhill. But we definitely are going to take advantage of it when we get the opportunity to. Yeah, he's he you know, he's another good example of a guy who's just getting a lot more confident and comfortable with what we're doing, what we're calling, how we're doing it. And you can see the difference when he's comfortable. Like my my man has some speed. You know, he's got juice. I think everybody can see it when he opens up. And it shows up more and more the more confident he is in in what exactly is going on around him. So, that's really what we're emphasizing with him. And then same deal. Like the run game's a run game. Always going to emphasize that for the backs. Can we grow in protection? Can we grow in the pass game? Can we shore up things like that? >> You called the play, I think, in walk-through, short out to Ali in the pass game. it stood out to me because there wasn't a lot of that today, and obviously it's minicamp, so it really doesn't matter at this point. But, running backs were used big-time in the pass game last year. If you were here, you know what H can do. Is there still going to be that heavy emphasis on that? Because there's a tendency with Malik to run instead of check down. You had a tendency in Houston to throw downfield and not utilize the running backs as much. So, I'm kind of curious how you you balance that. >> Yeah, I think it I think it goes back to like the initial conversation we had way back when I first got introduced here. Like, everything I try to do is keep a defense off balance. So, there absolutely is going to be part of that. And then, you know, you'll see some of it in walk-through when we're just trying to get a rep that won't show up in practice, and vice versa. Um but, we we want to do it all, you know? And then we're going to have this these core things we want to hang our hat on, but there's going to be times the back get out, and we emphasize the back getting out. We're going to use the run, we're going to use Ali, we're going to use J. Wright to get out, and they're they're the primary read. There's going to be other times they're out as a check down. There's going to be other times they're out as window dressing. There's going to be other times they're in a max pro. You know, we're going to we're going to mix it up pretty good. >> Are you emphasizing that to Malik to use those running backs in the passing game even more than he has in the >> Yeah, when it's when it's part of our like everything, when we're part of when it's part of our progression, part of the play, part of where we want the ball to potentially go, he knows that's that's a big part of what we're doing. >> Bobby, quick question. >> What have you learned about Keaton Mitchell so far? >> Yeah, it's it's probably a better question, honestly, for, you know, the the O-line guys, just the nature of OTAs. I'm with them a little less. I have been able to spend a a decent amount of time with him, though, and I've I've just liked his excitement for football. Like, he really wants to be a great player. Like, he doesn't just want to be good, he wants to be great. And that hunger you can see in him when he's out on the field right now. He practices like he's hungry. Um we got a lot to clean up and again a long way to go with all these guys with footwork, with hand placement, uh with scheme, but when you can see when the fundamentals, the hands are right, he I mean he has it in him. Like I mean it it is it is stout. It is powerful. Um so we're we're just excited to get all those guys out there and and really have the whole 11.

title: DC Sean Duggan meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: What's the indication you can get at this point as to how developed your pass rush can maybe get going into the training camp? >> Yeah, I mean, I think the guys are doing a good job. Again, we're still we're installing, right? We're installing the games we want to run, the pressures we want to run. I think you know, they're doing a great job in Indy working the techniques. Uh you know, it's a lot of it we still got to have pads on, right? I mean, rushes are way different with pads on than without. But, um the guys are working really hard at it. And I'm I'm excited to see the the progress they've made, how that continues in the camp. >> So, we know that a lot of football is situational. Without giving away any strategy, what have you learned about your linebackers in certain situations? Who first down, second down, etc. >> Yeah, um I think the you know, situationally I I think we we got to coach it number one, right? I think you need to talk to the guys about it. You know, we don't ever want to just take that for granted, but I think we have a lot of guys in that room who are very instinctual and understand the game from a situational perspective. Um which helps a lot, right? You know, third and 10, you better play a lot different than first and 10, right? Um Yeah, I think it's something you stress about. You Are you stressed during the meetings? You stress as you're installing. You know, I think when you when you install a call, the why behind each call, right? Are we calling this for pass? Are we calling this front to stop the run? What types of run are we want Do we want to take away when we're in this coverage? What does it take away? What are the weaknesses of it? Um so, I think as those guys learn that, you see that translate to the field and they can play faster and faster. >> And just at a glance, it seems like you have a lot of options, right? With your with situations as opposed to being restricted and saying I have to force this guy to do this. It's kind of like, how many things can this guy That's what it looks like to me. Is that accurate? >> I hope so. That's the goal. I hope it looks like that to the offenses, too. But, no. Well, I mean, we're trying to figure out what guys can do best, right? We're still learning these guys. Um And we we want to put them in the best position to showcase what they can do. And you know, which will lead to us playing good defense. >> Obviously, you guys don't know what you have but from a run stopping standpoint, without pads, but how do you evaluate the progress you're making in terms of that unit? >> Yeah, I think well, I think your point, I mean, it's I'm very thankful you said without pads. It's people always want to talk about the run game at OTAs. It's you know, this still isn't real football. So, I appreciate that. But, you know, you look at technique, right? You look at feet, you look at pad level, you look at hands, where are they placing their eyes? Do they understand what type of block they're getting? So, that when we get pads on, all those individual reps, all those reps we have out here without pads on, that can translate. So, you still see the same speed um and aggression, right? When they play the run with pads on. But, I think these guys are doing a nice job. I mean, it's hard to keep your pads down when you're a big guy. I think those guys are stressing. I think Coach Clark's doing a great job with those guys, especially up front. >> Without Chopper Robinson, he said he plans to play at 265. How much will the added weight make a difference? Is that the idea? >> You know, I I think it's a probably a better question for Chopper and the strength coaches, to be honest with you. I think, you know, you got to have some size to play up front. If you're talking about you're talking about run setting, setting the edge, right? Run game. I think size is always something you're going to need to have, but you also want the player to feel good, it it to be helpful for him and his body, you know? So, I think it's a good question for Todd. You can get Todd out here. >> You have been have been very complimentary of Chris Johnson. What have you seen from him? What stood out in the short time >> You know, number one is is just his enthusiasm out there every day. You know, he's the same guy every day. He's always happy. This is I think this is the best part of his day. And then you see a guy that's constantly growing, constantly getting better every single rep. You know, learning from mistakes and being able to to not make the same mistake twice. So, very happy with where Chris is. >> Jason Marshall Jr. seems to be stepping into more of a versatile role, working out of the slot the outside. How has he stood out to you so far? >> I I think it's the same as a lot of guys, right? They're they're working hard, they're being consistent every day and and not making the same mistake twice. You know, I think that's something we want to stress, right? As we've kind of the guys have a feeling of what we're doing right now, right? We've kind of dialed it back install-wise a little bit. We want to see guys play faster and you know, he's the same type of way as a lot of guys, who are not making the same mistake twice. >> I think it's Juju Brentz and his length really stands out to me on the field. What are some of the things that you look at that indicates to you that he can really take this next step? >> I think he's a he's a big man that's long and but has small man feet. You know, he can move, man. Um he's physical, you know, you watch his tape, he he plays the run. You know, he'll show up, he'll hit you, he'll he'll play like a big man out there, but he can move like a smaller guy. So, I'm I'm excited for Juju. He's another guy who's worked extremely hard. You know, he's been in here since we got here working and you know, I'm excited for him. >> What are the first things we need to know about Zane Anderson? Cuz you were also in in that room. And there's a different coach that does different things, but just what should we know about him and why he might be able to make some plays? >> Yeah, I think, you know, have you guys met Zane yet? Have you guys talked to him? Yeah, I mean, he's first off, he's an unbelievable person. You know, I think you guys probably got a glimpse of that. He's a great teammate, really cares for other people on the team. Um he's a guy that plays with unbelievable effort. He knows what he's doing. I mean, this guy when in Green Bay studied as much as anybody on the team. You know, when his number was called, he was ready for that. So, I think, you know, I'm excited to see him continue to take steps in his career. Um but can't say enough good things about Zane. >> Two more guys. >> With the revolving door at safety, what what guy opposite Dante, what are you looking for from that position? >> You know, I think right now it's it's all about competition, right? We're hopefully we're we're breeding that in that room and it should be really on the whole defense and the whole team. So, we're kind of we're looking for guys that can play fast, know the call, be in the right place. Um you know, safety you got to be able to play the run, but you also need to patrol the deep part of the field. >> And the quarterback >> One last question. >> Uh you haven't gotten to see Darrell Baker, okay, or Storm Duck. Uh what are they doing maybe off the the field that can get them prepared to compete once maybe training camp starts opening? >> Yeah, I I'm not I I can't really speak to what the the stuff they're doing and you know, they're working through their injuries and stuff like that. >> or more so just um you know, what's their outlook maybe to once they do get in there to uh in order to to fight for a spot? >> Come in and compete.

title: RB Ollie Gordon II meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: I would just say, you know, you don't really see backs at 6'2", 225, you know? So, I feel like once I get that momentum, get to move it downhill, not hard to get a yard or two, maybe three, you know? >> Is there anything you worked on during the off-season to prepare you for your second season in the NFL? >> Uh honestly, I would just say my speed, you know, trying to get, you know, drop a couple pounds, get a little faster. >> What's been your favorite part about being out here, just being back on the field? >> I would say building bonds with the teammates, you know? I feel like um getting to know everybody is the best part about this. Getting to know the coaches, too, that's good, too. You get to build bonds with them and the players. And I feel like once we stick together, we'll be fine. Uh I would just say I feel like we're more closer as a team. That's one, and you know, I I can't really tell you cuz this is my first time being here through the whole time. And I you know, last year I got drafted, so I didn't really know what was going on before. >> O.J., do you tell the coaches, and I know it's really on, you can accept more of a workload, or is it more where you show during these OTAs, and then once training camp starts and the pads come on? >> Yeah, it'll definitely it'll definitely just be showing more in OTAs, just showing, you know, I can handle that workload. You know, they trust me, they trust me. We'll figure that out when the time comes. Wait, can you repeat that? My bad, I'm sorry. I got you. I got you there. Uh-huh. I feel like really honestly, it's a mix of both, just because, you know, I'm bringing energy every day for sure. I feel like the whole team brings the energy. You know, sometimes you got you know, you got to let the quarterback lead that one, so I feel like I'll bring the energy for sure. >> O.J., in talking to Happily yesterday, he said two of the most important things he's done since he's been here are culture change and establishing a standard. What have you seen along those lines that that that backs that up? >> I would just say, you know, since day one half came in, he told us, you know, he was like, "We're going to be a team that's going to play together. We're going to be the most conditioned. We're going to do that." So, ever since then, you know, he he's definitely been on us chasing the ball down the field. So, he told us week one, and I mean, it's like what, a couple weeks down the road and and we're all chasing the ball now. So, I feel like that's one thing that has changed. I feel like he's giving us more time to build bonds with each other and become a team and actually, you know, get to know each other and build great bonds. >> He Today, he was telling us about the film sessions. He said he meets with you guys every day, 30 to 40 film clips, where he tells you what was good and and what was not so good. You're laughing. What Tell me about those film sessions. How are they? >> Nah, I feel like they're great just because, you know, you don't really want to be on the not so good side. So, I feel like when you're out there practice, you definitely thinking about it, going through, trying to be the best you could be. You know what I mean? When everybody doing the best they could be, we're doing something right. >> I noticed a smile on your face when I talked about the workload. What is it you want to from yourself in year two in the NFL? >> Uh you know, I feel like it's just too early to think about right now. Honestly, it's just >> What do you envision? >> Uh I mean, that's a huge question, honestly. It's just I'm not really thinking about that right now. Right now, my mind is here in OTAs, trying to get everything down, you know, still working through that. I mean, it's a bunch of stuff that has to lead up to that before I can even answer that question. >> How do you feel this year coming into camp because we know after your last year of college, right, you're training for the combine and pro day and all that. This offseason, you get to work on football stuff. So, how how better prepared are you this this OTAs and mini camp be? >> Man, I feel like I'm way more prepared than I was last year. I don't have to run track, you know what I'm saying? >> [laughter] >> But now, it's definitely better just because I've been here the whole time. I didn't have to worry about getting drafted, get on a flight, coming out I get where I'm going to stay, where I'm going to live, you know, all that. So, I feel like you know, being here the whole time has been great, honestly. Oh, I'm loving it. You know, this is my number in college. I don't think I could do the 31 no more.

title: CB Chris Johnson meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Obviously, you've done it before, but what is it like doing it at this level and then what does it say to have these wings to, you know, entrust you doing all that? >> Yeah, it's definitely interesting doing it at at this level. I feel like back in school when I did it, I was kind of just playing like man-to-man in there, but coming here and actually learning the zone drops and learning, you know, the different kinds of coverages is you know, it's you know, it's not easy, but I'm getting it done. You know what I mean? And uh like you said, uh coach Haf being able to put me in that position just says he he views views me as a very important player to be able to do important things for playing inside and outside. So, you know, there's just a lot of pressure on me, but like I said, like I enjoy pressure and you know, I I like to come out on top. >> When we talked to Haf earlier today, he was really emphasizing the importance of effort. >> Mhm. >> Um from your perspective, what's been kind of his message over there for >> Yeah, really just effort, man. Just getting to the ball. I feel like good things happen to players who get to the ball, um which is something that we emphasized back at San Diego State, so it's really none to me. Um and you know, I've seen it firsthand. Guys running to the ball, uh a fumble might pop out, a ball might tip up in the air. If you weren't running to the ball, you won't make that play and every ball in the air is money. So, just emphasizing that, you know, he wants to be he wants to be plus in in turnover diff, so you know, that's what we got to try to do. >> And you've been a young guy, what's been the most surprising thing or the thing that's happened here that you didn't expect being at the >> Yeah, really just uh just how helpful everybody is. You know, we already got a brotherhood in in in the corner room or or as DBs in general and you know, coming in you think like guys are are going to dislike you for whatever reason or you know, different kind of rumors that you've heard growing up, but everybody here has welcomed me with open arms and nobody keeps any secrets from anybody. If I got to ask anybody anything to help me, they'll help me, vice versa.

Good length, good size, he could press, get his hands on people at the line of scrimmage. Though I'd be lying if we say we didn't put him on the inside at all. Actually, on some third down plays, we did put him on the inside. Um, but primarily he has and will be on the outside for us. And I think he's done a really good job. I think when the pads come on, which I keep saying, we we'll find out um how much improvement he has made um in tackling, the physicality, playing at the line of scrimmage, and all that stuff. But um I I like his demeanor. I like the way he's gone about the off season and I I can look in the eye and tell you I'm excited about him as a player. >> I want to ask you about uh Jordan Phillips. I think Zack Cer joked last week that he got trouble for squatting too much. What's been the most impressive part about what how he looks right now coming out of the offseason? >> Just like you said, he's strong. I think it's hard to see really how much improvement he's made because the lack of physicality in our practices and I don't think he's a player that's going to kind of jump out as much when the pads aren't on and he's not taking on double teams and you know trying to stuff the run. But you can just see how strong he is and you can see how violent he is in practice whether he's on a sled or in his drill work. Um, you know, but the thing I'll say about him is I, you know, I think it was probably the day after I got hired. He is in the weight room on days off and he he embraces playing the run and he embraces double teams and he embraces the dirty work which most people in our league don't like to do. He's an unselfish player who truly loves to play this game. Um and again I'm very excited to see him when we actually start playing real football. >> Could you see him as a zero technique? >> Him? Absolutely. Yeah. I think I think he's a damn good zero technique. I think he thrives the closer he gets to the center and he plays with more head-up techniques. Um, and you know, I'm not going to I'm not going to knock him as a pass rusher. That's not what I'm doing. Hopefully that will improve and and he'll have some production in that regard. Uh, but I think he'll be a really good zero. >> I have a hard-hitting question for you here. >> Hard hitting? >> Yeah, it's very hard-hitting. Who selects the music for practice? >> Um, Joe. >> Joe selects it. There were the concert throughout the year or tweet. >> I don't know who selects it. Joe asked me if I had anything specific I wanted to hear and I told him to play whatever he wanted. So maybe he does select it. Maybe he asked the players or someone else who selects it. When I get tired of hearing it, you'll probably hear some Springsteen and you'll know that I chimed in. >> I don't even notice the music's going on. The only thing I asked is certain periods it's turned down a little bit so we can hear us coaching and certain periods when it's not needed, turn it up. But I don't I couldn't tell you a song that played. I don't even know music's out there. So, unless it gets too loud and I can't get my message across. So, but let's say Joe picks it. Am I right in saying that, Andy? Or wrong? >> Wrong. >> I say Joe picks it. >> That's another one along the same lines. How is the the the placement of the player during the stretching period determined? >> Most of it's by position or if a guy specifically wants to stand stand somewhere, he can. I think Brewer is the only one who kind of likes to hang out where the D linemen are, which I think is pretty cool. So, I don't say anything to him about it. Those are the things though, like as as long as guys are lined up and where they're supposed to be. I mean, we're not going to win or lose a game by if Brewer wants to hang out with the Dline. So, I'm not sure. >> This is a You're making me think of things that >> because there were some defensive guys who were with the offensive players. That's why it's not just >> as long as they're doing their job and they're stretching. >> They can stand wherever they want. >> We've watched stretching for quite a while. You're probably the longest stretch I've ever seen like 20 minutes. Not to say this is a bad thing. Is that something that goes back to Green Bay, Boston College or >> um I think I think probably more Green Bay. I think there's some studies now, especially with ACL's that there's certain exercises if you do and protocols that you follow um that they've talked to us a lot about. I think, you know, it increases our chances not to have those injuries. So, I think I know we're taking that very seriously. So, as long as we are stretching and sometimes it gets frustrating for you and me because we just want to start practice and you guys probably want to leave. Um, I think it's really important to do. So, that's been very intentional to try to follow those guidelines so we can, you know, maximize our ability for our players to stay healthy. >> Sure. >> It is long. is very long. >> Short yardage was kind of a problem for the team for a few years and Ali Gordon early last year kind of helped solve that issue big back obviously and then it kind of tailed off. I'm curious your opinion on third and one fourth and one from your experience what usually determines whether a team has success in that area throughout a season. >> Oh, that's a good question because usually I'm looking at it from the opposite side of the ball. I think it's tricky right now. I think it's where you are on the field. When I think of third down and short yardage, third and one, especially third and one, it's where are you on the field? I think if you're if you're on the minus side of the field, a lot of the times you still have the option to run your, you know, your your big people got to get the yard. Um, you know, less inclined to throw the ball than you are if you get close to the 50 on the plus side of the field when your playbook's kind of opened up because there's a good chance you're going to go for it on fourth down. So now you're treating third and one like fourth and one where on the minus side of the field third and one is third and one. Um so it depends. I mean I'd have to study what they did here in the past, but a lot of teams will get in the bigger personnel groupings and run the ball and try to get you downhill. A lot of teams will go under center and sneak the quarterback. A lot of teams will, you know, a lot of teams on third and one will get the quarterback under center if teams get in the sneak defense and they'll try to get you on a perimeter play. So there's a lot of cat and mouse that goes into that and that we have to think about a lot of the times. Do we want to call something then he comes out under center and get into a sneak front because the quarterback's just going to get up to the line of scrimmage and sneak the ball and if he sees the two guys in the a gaps is he going to try to get something on the perimeter. Um but short yardage has become tricky especially on the plus side of the field because it's more like second one and teams are taking shots so we can't be as aggressive on defense. So stay out of third and fourth and one on defense and try to get into it on offense and um it's hard to stop. >> How long the show? What's your thoughts feelings on the push push? >> It's hard to stop. So get good at it and do it. I mean it it's really hard to stop. So as long as it's a legal play, we need to figure out on defense a way to stop it. And with a quarterback like we have with Malik um and some big guys up front, maybe we can get good at it. >> When we're out there at practice, we see a lot of interaction and a lot of uh teaching coach to player, coach to coach and player to player. In your opinion, I know this a young team and first year staff. Is there more of that this year with this team than you have maybe in Green Bay or anything along those we see more of that do you think? Uh, no. I think anywhere that I've been or any staff that I've been a part of or had a leadership role in, I think I think that's huge. I just, you know, for me it's always been and in our I'll kind of talk from a sense of a DB coach, right? Because it's what I was for most of my career. Stuff that would drive me nuts would be like a guy gets beat on a go ball or a touchdown and a coach just starts yelling. I mean, what are you yelling at? Like the guy got beat and it sucks, right? Go coach him and ask him what he saw, why he saw what he did, what he did on his first step, where his eyes were. Pick his brain on why he did what he did. Why was he in a trail position, why wasn't he on top, why did he finish the way he did? Why didn't he turn back? Why'd he play through the front shoulder? Listen to him and then tell him what you saw and what he could do to correct it. And I think there has to be that constant communication, right? There's times when someone makes a great play and on this side of the of the field or an interception and while the whole team's going to celebrate over there, I'm going to talk to this DB over here because he completely busted the coverage and there was a guy wide open down there. So, while the result was good, the process could have been terrible because he didn't do his job on the backside. So, it's constant feedback and coaching and teaching because I do think a lot of the times if you get the feedback fast, it sticks longer, right? I think going to the film room is really important because then you can really spend the time to teach and some coaches don't like a lot of teaching on the field because they just want to go go go which is fine. I would just rather give constant feedback and constant communication as long as it doesn't hold up practice. And it's the same thing in practice with coaches. If I see something, I'll I'll ask a coach to come over and have a conversation and ask why he did what he did or why he called what he called or what he's teaching there. Did he see what happened or say something else that I saw? >> Ju yesterday spoke pretty excitedly about how often you work with the defensive backs and the feedback that you give them. I know you're kind of getting used to being everywhere around the practice field, but what is that experience like for you whenever you do go back to the defensive backs considering your your background equation and position? Yeah, it's it's usually when things get going, it's usually where my eyes go first and I have to usually fight not to look there because I've done it for so long. And you know, if I could pick one meeting to sit in and I have to go around and sit in them all, I'd rather be in the DB DB meeting. And having Downer and Mile and and those guys in there and and shed, it's awesome. And I think they've done a really good job and they're really good coaches and I have spent a lot of time in that room. But there's also some specific things that I want coached a certain way that I truly believe in. So, I'm gonna help use, if you want to call it, my expertise in that position to help everybody. Um, but usually it's what I see the quickest. It's what I see the most and I usually like to give those guys a ton of feedback and help them. But I also know we have three good coaches in that room and I want them to coach. But I love working with the DBs. I just I think you'll probably see me around that group more as training camp starts. I'm trying to fight it and go to other groups right now, but eventually I'll be there more. >> If I could follow up, we get to talk to to Chris after practice today at >> Johnson. Chris on the team, >> but uh >> maybe there might not be any. >> Do we have other Chrises on >> Chris? Chris Bell. >> Yeah, Chris Bell. >> I bet you we have more if we want to go up and down the whole roster. So, I apologize to any Chrises if we don't. >> Chris Taber. >> You got any more for me? Look at him holding his phone hoping that >> But it's Chris Johnson quarterback San Diego State today. And uh just curious, considering how much you like him coming in the draft, what's the feedback been from you uh through these first few months on the field? >> I think he's done a really nice job. Um, he is very instinctual. He sees the game very fast. He works really hard in the meeting rooms. He's super athletic, has really good coverage ability. Um, he's been able to get his hand on the football and, um, we've asked him to do a lot and he's handled it very, very well. Um, which is what I kind of told you maybe a week or two ago. We've thrown a lot on his plate and he's responded and I'm really excited to continue to coach him. I think you guys will like him a lot when you talk to him. Um he he's got a good energy about him and he's mature. He's you'll see it. He's really immature for a rookie. >> Coach, remember back in the winter the press conference you talked about using late season tape and late in games, maybe you're out of the playoffs to kind of gauge guys efforts. Are you doing that constantly at practice out here? And do you clock it live in the moment or is that a film room thing? >> Effort. I watch effort when I watch uh the film on every single play and then I show them in there. Today I showed them great examples of effort and I called out guys for great effort and I I meet with the team every morning and I go through probably 30 to 40 clips on both sides of the ball and I talk about ball security. I talk about taking the ball away. I talk about fundamentals and technique. I pull out plays on both sides of the ball and I show good execution, poor execution, why it happened. I try to show the offense how the defense made a mistake and the defense how the offense took advantage of it and I try to teach. But then it all comes back to the most important thing I show them is effort. And I'll show defensive guys running to the ball on the backside. I'll show a defensive lineman putting his foot in the ground and retracing to the ball. And I'll show them that. And I'll call guys out by name. I'll call them out by number. And I'll applaud them for that because when they do that, and I've said this before, it shows me how much they care about their teammates. And then conversely, I'll show a guy who didn't run to the ball and I'll challenge them and I'll ask him why. And I'll tell them that that's not good enough. And I don't do it in an an insulting way. I just continually show guys what I see. And I'm trying to teach him what's good enough and what's not good enough. On offense, it's the same way. When a wide receiver catches the ball, the other wide receiver on the backside better put his foot in the ground and go block for him to show him that he cares about him and he's unselfish and that he loves his teammates and he's going to play for his teammates. And the same thing when I don't see that I'm going to call it out. And today there were probably the most we've had on offense. Guys are starting to learn to transition. Oh, I didn't get the ball. I'm going to flip and go find somebody in block form so we can score touchdowns. So that is the most important thing to me. I cannot always see that on the field, but if I do, I will immediately grab a guy and tell him that that's not good enough. Um, just as I think it's important for guys to jog on and off the field. I just think it's a habit that when you're out there and you're on the field playing the game, it's a respect thing and and it's a conditioning thing. And all of that stuff is really important to me because I do believe it helps win games. >> Good. >> I'll see you guys three days in a row.

title: Is a $98K Holdout Worth It?
text: So, let's jump into this next 3 days mandatory mini camps. First and foremost, do you guys expect any holdouts? Do you think Brewer is going to hold out? I don't think Brooks will because if he would have, he would have not been at OTAAS. Um it's um >> called doing my job. >> It's called voluntary work. I'm not going to penalize or call somebody out for being not being there during voluntary work, even though the culture encourages it. I'm not a person who believes in being forced by the culture to do anything. Um, >> player agent, I'm sorry. >> Uh, here's the thing. If, let me speak directly to to Aon Brewer. Um, but at the same time, you know, it just becomes your reality really.
