title: Rylie Mills: "I'm Fully Back To Who I Was Before The Injury" | Seattle Seahawks
text: What's going on? >> How you doing, Riley? How much better does it feel being healthy this season? >> Way more fun. >> Yeah, it's a lot more fun when you can uh you're not just standing behind everybody just mentally going through drills. >> What was it being able to have the sack of the Super Bowl kind of the reaction to that? What I guess looking back on that, what was that kind of that you were able to have that moment despite what happened to you not being able to play most of the year? Yeah, I you know, looking back at it, I feel like, you know, my takeaway is it kind of just felt like the end of like a a long chapter like in my career. Like I felt like from the like the start of the injury and the rehab process, like you go through so many different phases. And uh you know, the ultimate goal is to get back and get back to who I was, you know, before the injury. And so I think just that moment like you know, I think a couple days thinking after I was like, man, that really was like a story book kind of ending on it. But I feel like I closed that chapter and I'm ready to to get going and for this next chapter to start. How beneficial was it Friday that they just didn't put you on injured reserve and and you got the opportunity to stay engaged and then paid off to play? Yeah, I mean I think it's a shout out to the staff for having that kind of belief in me and you know the guys upstairs and you know our coaches. I think, you know, that means the world to me that they have that confidence and, you know, I know it's tough to take a guy that, you know, tore his ACL a couple, you know, months ago before the draft. And, you know, I think it just shows the kind of program we have here where it's like guys can come in and, you know, you put your all into it and, you know, especially with CJ and Strick and those guys with the rehab process, you know, I never felt like coming out there that I wasn't ready. So, I had full confidence and to, you know, see that from the other side is, you know, means the world to me. >> Today, how close do you feel like you are to where you were before? Yeah, I feel 100% like I feel great. You know, it's been nice having uh you know, that offseason just to kind of get back to working out and get my body back, but it feels great. I feel like a whole different player than I was, you know, when I first came back. >> How many times Go ahead. >> Do you feel like this is your rookie year or how you being treated by the guys? Are you still a rookie? How does that work? >> I feel like it's been nice because I'm kind of like treated like a second year guy, but I think I'm trying to take the rookie approach. It's like I don't know everything. Um, you know, so I'm definitely I have stuff to learn uh all the time, but I luckily I'm, you know, not having to do any of the rookie dues or sing any uh any more songs. >> How many times have you gone back and watched that sack? >> Uh I watched it a couple, maybe more than a couple. I've seen it uh a few times. It was cool. It It was just awesome. And it's funny because I don't remember the play at all. Like I kind of just blacked out and went and you know, just remembered after the play celebrating, but it's cool to like look back and like, man, that worked out, you know, perfect. I'm sure you saw a lot of the the clips of it from your teammates on the bench kind of seeing it and celebrating and everything. What was that kind of like to go back and see their reaction and being pretty hyped for you in that moment to be able to get a part of that? >> Yeah, I think that's the coolest thing of all time. Like just seeing my teammates hyped up for me like that that always gets me going just seeing the guys hyped up. When I came to the sideline I was like you have everyone smacking your helmet and hyping you up. Like that's the coolest thing ever. Uh I think EJ even even knocked me over after the play trying to celebrate. Um, but it was awesome to see that kind of support and, you know, they've watched me do all the rehab process and try to be locked in. So, it's it was great to see that. >> Like you said, last year your goal was just to get back all the way get all the way back healthy. What's been the driving force behind your off season, a normal off season, now getting into your pseudo rookie season? What's been your driving force? >> Yeah, I think for me it's just, you know, taking this opportunity and trying to run with it. Um, you know, coming back from the injury, I feel like now I'm I'm fully back to myself and fully back to who I was before the injury. So, you know, I want to step in that role and, you know, be a player that gets better every day. You know, for me, it's just about that improvement and, you know, I know not everything's going to be perfect, but, you know, I want to get better each and every day that I'm out here. >> Is the way they want to use you here, how you were used in Notre Dame and all that, or is there going to be any kind of differences at all how they're using? >> Yeah, it's pretty similar. I think there's a little more end. I think there's, you know, the thing that's interesting about me is I get to play kind of all different positions down the line. So, and I love that because it kind of gives me an opportunity at, you know, any spot because that's how, you know, it kind of goes in the season. So, I've been able to learn a ton and, you know, learn from AD and Hind. I feel like I've uh I've really grown my game a lot and been learning a lot. >> You've been getting to line up next to Byron Murphy a fair amount during practice. What kind of damage do you think you guys can do as a pair? >> It's I mean you guys have already seen what Murf does. Like that dude's a freak. Um so it's great because every time I play next to him I know something crazy is going to happen. So you know I can play off him and you know I think make a great group inside and he's been a guy that's spoken up a ton this off seasonason. So he's been a really good leader and you know I just try to follow him. He leads by example. >> In a rookie season that you were rehabing a while. How valuable having veterans like Jerry or you know just learn? >> It was super helpful because like when I came to the NFL like you everything in college is in the gun and you know here everything was under center. So I I had a lot to learn and you know I think the bright side you know of being in that injury spot is I got to sit there and you know I could watch the plays on offense and kind of get some of the looks and then I could ask Leo or Jay Reed or you know Law any of the older guys you know kind of about them and you know what I'm seeing. So I got to learn a ton and you know they were a great help and I couldn't you know say thanks more. >> What's it like? You didn't have a training camp. Obviously, those first couple games back kind of were your training camp in your preseason. What What were the biggest lessons that you learned those first couple games kind of getting thrown in the fire in a playoff race? >> Man, they ran wham the first play. Like I was like ready to fire off the ball and they ran wham and I was like, "Oh my god." So I think uh keep your head on a swivel. Uh no, I got to learn a ton. I think, you know, definitely it's different when you go from starting a week 15 practice to a live game, but I kind of I feel like I learned best kind of getting thrown in the fire and, you know, it ended up working out great, but yeah, definitely a bit of an adjustment. >> What's it like practicing this time of the year and seems like having to kind of dial yourself back at times trying to keep everything within the rules and all that? >> It's it's it's been good. It's adjustable. I like to use my power. So, I feel like here you kind of you can't use your power, you got to use other things. So, it's actually it's forced me to grow in other areas, but there's definitely times where like I'll get mad and just try to go to power and you know AD's got to be like, "Hey, chill out. Just work your hands." Um, so it's been a bit of an adjustment. >> What did you learn about yourself throughout the rehab process as you were working your way to get back? >> Uh, what I learned about myself, I just think I'm mentally tougher than I thought. And I think I was prepared for it. And, you know, I think going through the process, I think a lot of people would have broke. I think it would have been a tough thing to deal with, you know, having an ACL injury like to what mine was. And I think a lot of people would have quit or not seen the light at the end of the tunnel. And so I think one thing I learned is that no matter the uh the obstacle or the challenge, it's just one day at a time. And you know, the opportunity may not come tomorrow or the next day, but eventually when it comes, you're either be ready for it or you're not. >> I appreciate it.

title: Cooper Kupp: "We're Just Going To Keep Getting Better" | Seattle Seahawks
text: What's up everyone? >> Fantastic. >> Sam something similar yesterday, but how much different does this feel for you guys all being together for a full year versus last year? You were new quarterbacks knew the offenses so much. >> Yeah, I can't speak for everyone, but I know for me personally coming in knowing people, knowing how to get around the facility, knowing how to get to the facility, like all those things like uh having a house, having having a home, all those things, it's uh that felt very different this year. And um obviously knowing a little bit about uh the guys, how you know how things are run here, how Mike operates, how we operate as a team and um all that stuff, all the stuff that goes into functioning at a high level and just being a little bit ahead. Um definitely helpful. >> Did you give any thoughts to maybe going out on top? >> Oh, no. Never for a second. I'm I'm I'm loving playing this game too much and um I I just uh I love playing football and so like I'm I'm enjoying it and um yeah, so no that was never a thought. >> The message is run it forward, but this is the second time you've won a Super Bowl in the locker room. What do you guys take away from the knowledge that you got to >> um I don't know. I mean, there's always like like no matter what happens from one year to the next, there's going to be good and there's going to be bad. And I think that we what you don't want to fall into is this idea of thinking that just because something worked that it was the best way of doing things. Um but at the same time, there's the balance of knowing that um if something did work, sometimes it's best not to fix something that was working. So, all that being said, it's like you you treat this just like any other year. You you look at the things that um you look at your film. You look at the process. You look at, you know, your what you put on tape and what you uh what your year was the year before. You identify things that can get better. Uh you scrutinize. Um and then, you know, you build on those things all offseason and you try to attack the weaknesses. Um you know, like regard like you don't look at the results at all. I think I that's just kind of the um that's the best way to do it because that's what you've done. All these guys that are in this building have done that year after year for their entire lives. That's why you're playing in the NFL right now is because you've continually found ways to get better and you know take that same approach regardless of what the result was. It's like, hey, we can get better. We can scrutinize. We can be um we can dive into things and um just because something worked um that doesn't mean that we can't still find ways to improve on it. >> On that same note, how How do you maintain that consistency when you have a new offensive coordinator this year from last year? >> Yeah. Well, um you know there's a certain standard of operation that we you know live by and um a mentality that you have when you step in this building. And so you know part of it is just you know carrying through that like like that that needs to stay the same. Um and being in a headsp space being a uh uh bringing energy to allow the work to get done that's going to allow you to get better. Um, you know, Brian's done an unbelievable job of um himself meeting that standard and coming in with an ability to challenge people and um push people, find ways to tinker and find the ways to get the best out of people and and recognizing personnel what the strengths and weaknesses are here. And um he's been uh he's been awesome in terms of just how he's installing things and the detail of all that. So, uh we're just going to keep getting better and um there is a the way that you keep continuity is by continuing to keep that same energy, that same process. Um, and uh, coming ready to work. >> Last year, if I remember correctly, I think you described Clint Kubak as someone who was pulled off a ranch in Texas to be an NFL coordinator. >> I think so. Yeah. I hope I'm not misquoting you, but how would you describe Brian Flurry? >> Um, yeah. Uh, I mean, he's I thought Clint was so uh, you know, calm, softspoken, how he like went about like there's times like there's going to be fiery moments and um, things like that, but I thought he was so calm and collected on all stuff and like Brian's given Clint to run for the money in terms of that same demeanor of just like, hey, there's going to be a there's just a clear understanding and so there's not a there's no jittery energy. There's no like false energy. It's just, hey, this is this is what I know to be true. This is how we're going to, you know, execute it. These are my expectations. Then we go out there and make it happen. Then we'll make corrections and move forward. And so, um, he allows guys, I think you allow a lot of freedom in that. Um, guys just play free and let it go because, you know, there's going to be someone that knows what they're talking about and, uh, is ready to coach you in that regard. So, um, he's been awesome in that way. Um, I don't have a geographical location for you from where he came from, but, um, but he's been great. How do you how did you put last year kind of in perspective when you just think about, you know, coming to a new team and all that you went through with that ended up in the Super Bowl and all that? >> Yeah, I mean it was a it was um it was a really cool journey. Um incredible like looking back on all the highs and lows and things like that. Um but yeah, I mean it's just it's like all that being said, it's just it's great being here now, being here with the guys, understanding that there's a relationship, there's just uh there is a lot of continuity going into this year. um a lot of built trust um and uh and camaraderie that's I think has carried in and made you know coming here this year um you know some a really good feeling kind of heading into OTAAS and the work that we put in how Super Bowl teams work and guys get paid in the league and all are you surprised at how much continuity they were able to retain upstairs for this year >> um I don't know about surprised I mean have like uh I think we I think this is a fun place to come work I think it's a fun fun um organization to be a part of and got a lot of really good people here and uh you know you come to work and you've got if you want to be about the right stuff you're going to be around a lot of the right people um here and so u I think that you know breeds like it's like man this is something that's it's not like that everywhere you know I've heard I've only been two places but I've heard horror stories um thankfully never had to live in those places but Um it's uh there's a few places I know around the league that are are unique in that way and u I think we've got a little bit of a an uncommon thing here. >> What goes through your mind when you walk in here and you see the banner up there? >> Yeah, I don't know. I mean it was uh it's cool. It's like there's there's moments of reflection, right? Um there's moments of understanding that um you each of these banners that's up in the up here is like there's a a story and uh a lot of you know blood, sweat, and tears behind each of them. And so there's a there's like that the respect for what went into those things and and what those stand for and the journey that they stand for. Um the hardships that were overcoming each of those things, but um it's also like at the end of that like moment of reflection is like the the period at the end that says like well like like now what you know and it's like this is yeah that's what it took. this is what like that that was and now you're in it and you're moving forward and there's an opportunity to go and um be a part of another one, experience what it's like to go and um chase after something um really special like that. >> Do do you remember I guess what the biggest challenge was when you went through this with the Rams when they won the Super Bowl? >> Uh from one year to the next? >> Yeah. >> Yeah. I mean those it's so unique, right? Like um you know it's so unique. we the you know back in 22 like the the injuries and things that were going on um I we weren't able like we were out here you know we've been out here for however I can't I don't even want to say the amount of time we've been out here for the max allotted amount of time for OTAAS and like and competing the whole time you know and we weren't even like we weren't capable of doing that in 2022 in LA because we had just too many injuries we got like we couldn't do it um so it's very different right in terms of how like what's your approach in that regard and um what's been great is just being able to come back here and and guys are healthy, guys are competing. Um and uh it's been like it's been some really good work um you know moving forward and like I said being able to chase them especially here the importance of having honest discussion when you're building a challenging environment that continues to build. Can you talk about that? >> Yeah. Well, I mean shoot just like anything that's worth going through is going to be difficult. if it's easy, you're gonna get to the end of the you're at the end of that journey and uh whatever you're holding at the end of that, it's not going to hold much weight. And it's just that's just how life seems to be. And it's like uh my wife and I take that same approach in our marriage in terms of having hard conversations and not running away from difficult things and being able to face them head-on together. And uh in the same way and I I want my marriage to be great. In the same way you want an organization to be great, you got to be able to tell the truth to each other. Uh you got to be able to have hard conversations. You got to be able to model those things and be accepting of the fact that like there's going to be times that you do fall short and when you do get called on it, be able to look at yourself in the mirror and say like, "Yeah, that was that was wrong." And and we're going to find a way to, you know, get through it and find the uh way we want to operate. And so, um, regardless of whatever successes have happened, regardless of whatever, like I said, whatever result is, we win a game, just because you win a game doesn't mean there aren't some good hard conversations that need to happen on that Monday morning about things that we need to do better as guys are going to get coached hard. Um, because the result doesn't change what the process was, right? Like, like we want to be about the process. about be about challenging ourselves to be the best day in and day out to give ourselves the best chance at a positive outcome. text: How's everybody doing? >> Pretty good. >> What are you going through right now physically? >> Um, just a little soreness in my shoulder. Everything's clean and looks good. Like we have a good football team and we're going to be healthy this year and um have a chance to do some good stuff. >> In the bank last year, how important was that for you just to establish that or reestablish yourself in that way? >> Yeah, for sure. It was good. I think um it was important for me just to have fun and get get around this group of guys and have the continue to be with these guys because it's a good group in the locker room and got a lot of older guys but now we have some younger guys too and I feel like I'm kind of in the middle. You kind of just got to be where your feet are and I know that I can play in the system and I know that I can play even better in the system and I got good support from coach Kyle and Clay and and everybody. title: Minicamp Wrap Up with Pat Freiermuth | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Hi everybody, I'm Missy Matthews joined by Mike Pursuda and Pat Fri kind enough to join us as veteran mini camp winds down. A few OTAAS left, but Pat, we probably won't see you maybe until Latroe when training camp starts. How has the process been getting acclimated to not only a new coaching staff, but also some new teammates as well? >> I mean, just like every single year you go into it with a with a fresh mind. Um, you know, obviously it's different this year cuz we have a new head coach, but and a whole new staff, but um, they've done a great job of I've thought of of blending the culture. You know, we've already had an established winning culture in Pittsburgh. And so, um, we're just looking to add to that. And I think coach has done a great job of implementing him his system and his core values into the values we already had in the building. So, it's been great. You know, Mike comes in with a pretty wellestablished reputation as a quarterback guy, a passing game guy, and we keep hearing everybody talk about running the ball, and how significant that's going to be. How do you see the offense? I don't know if evolving is the right word or shifting, >> what's what's going to be the signature, and how diverse do you expect it to be? >> Yeah, I mean, I like any offense, you obviously want to to set up the run game and the play action. Those are where the explosive plays come. You're going to want be able to run the ball. Um it's tough to see what we have in the in the run game with what's going on right now with the limitations. Um it's really truly just a passing camp. Um so you know we're getting the installs down with the new pass concepts and and the timing and stuff like that. But when we get to LRO and put the pads on, we're able to see, you know, what we're good at in the run game and and then you'll really be able to see the the offense evolve. >> I know everybody was excited last year about Aaron Rogers coming for year two. A chance to build off of what you guys did last year. What have you seen in terms of him maybe being different or more comfortable or I don't know what the word would be with Mike McCarthy now being the head coach? >> Yeah, he um he seems comfortable. You know, he he's just been consistent ever since he's been here, you know, especially last year. Obviously, him being new to to Mike T in the building. He done a but at the end of the day, it's Aaron Rogers. So, he did a great job of of coming in here and kind of learning his way and finding his routine. But, you know, he it was great. in coming to this year. Obviously, he has he's been familiar with coach McCarthy and his and that scheme. So, it's been kind of cool to see him remember things from the past, show up old clips and and kind of to really detail in on the stuff that he um has done a lot in the past. So, uh it's been cool to work with him and personally, I'm just excited to have the quarterback a quarterback for this backto-back years. >> Yeah. It's something new, huh? >> Yeah. >> Yeah. Mike McCarthy had mentioned to us at least that uh he thought Aaron Rogers on the first OTI. He came out and made sure everybody knew he still got the arm. >> Yeah. Has there been a moment or two out here where he thought, "Yep, that's uh that's what he that's who he is and that's what he does." >> Yeah. I mean, the past two days he's hit a a field post at DK and Roman. So, it's been pretty impressive to see that he still has all the the juice left in his arm. So, uh it's been cool to see him out here having fun. Um, I mean, I'm sure he's he's excited about all the the things to come this year and just cool to be able to experience another year with him. >> Not just the offense, but uh you're a second contract guy. Nick Herbe got a second contract. Just building this new young core that is a little bit different than what you were known previously when you started here with the Steelers when it was more veteran heavy. What's it like having that group of guys and trying to build your own thing? >> Yeah, it's really cool. Cool. I mean, I think the cool thing with Pittsburgh is, you know, they draft really well and and they reward their guys with second contracts if they if they earn it and and Herb has certainly earned that. Super happy for him and I'm just super happy for the guys that have earned those contracts. Um to able to be able to build together um be familiar with each other and really kind of create a culture of of what they what we believe in. Learning from guys like Cam and TJ, Alex, uh Jaylen, just all those vets. um learning from the culture that they learned from from Troy and Ben. >> We had talked I can't remember if it was the first or second week of OTAAS, but you mentioned that the memorable thing last year was winning a division and getting a home playoff game. What do you guys need to do collectively to make the memorable thing winning playoff game >> right now? Really just honeing on the details. Um, and then when we get into the season, being able to be adaptable to to what defense is doing to us and just be able to create explosive plays, you know, be able to utilize the personnel that, you know, that we have and, you know, I think it will all come together. And I think we just need to continue to build on the details that we've been doing and when we that way when we get into those high pressurized moments in big time games, we can lean back on our training. >> Can you start to envision at this early juncture the difference a Michael Pitman Jr. and a Jeremy Bernard can make in your passing attack? >> Yeah, man. It's been cool to be out there um with all the the the skill we have on on the outside in the in the interior of the the offense. You know, me and Darnell and Pitman, DK, Ro and Jeremy. It's been it's been really fun to to be a part of that in the huddle and seeing all the talent we have. Just super excited for this year and I think it will be a very successful year. >> You already talked about Aaron Rogers. You know Mason Rudolph well, Will Howard as well, but not so much in a game setting. Um, what have you seen not only from Mason, but Will Howard and the rookie Drew Aller? >> Seen a lot. Obviously, you know, this this camp is is good for them to to learn the new system and get reps and and and get some reps under their belt. Um, I think Will's done a great job of of coming in and kind of, you know, learning from Aaron and creating his own way. And same with Mason. I mean, I've been his team this probably my longest teammate that I've had. So, and Drew, it's it's been cool to kind of work with a Penn State guy. And >> And you're going to say that >> 100%. And uh it's just been cool to see him here. He's been, you know, first couple days as a as a as a pro is is really tough on a rookie. New team, new building, and it's been tough, but he's been really progressing really well, and it's just been he led the team down on a two-minute drive the other day, and uh it's just great to see him get more comfortable in the locker room and offense. >> Do you guys have any idea what camp's going to be like yet, or are you going to kind of go through this whole well, let's figure it out as we go along type of process? >> Just figure it out how we go along, and I'm going to be the same boat as you guys, and just take a day at a time. All right, Pat, thanks for joining us. Mike, thanks as always. Uh, that is a wrap on the veteran mini camp for the Pittsburgh Steelers here at the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex.
